assumptions_and_risks: Issue #70 is currently open with no prerequisites and live body matches supplied immutable original; re-read at every harness gate/publication boundary.

Worker-wide means all compilation threads/contexts in this replay process; unrelated child activity must not keep a stalled child alive. Any completed work resets only that worker dispatcher no-progress observation.

Multiple-thread dequeue order does not guarantee completion order; fixture barriers must hold the awaited context and prove actual other-context completions before advancing controlled dispatcher time.

Existing ReplayDeadline monotonic elapsed/overshoot semantics from #16 replace the historical counted wakeups in issue research patch; implement against current production semantics, not by applying the old patch blindly.

No proprietary input is necessary for acceptance. Synthetic successful creations and read-back parent inputs establish the bounded shared scheduling defect only, not GPU performance or Steam launch speedup.
If mandatory Linux prerequisites or assertion-bearing cases cannot be executed, report incomplete/unable_to_verify and route environment/design findings rather than weakening gates.

assertions: Include shipping cli/fossilize_replay.cpp and call the actual sync_worker_memory_context(PARENT_PIPELINE_MEMORY_CONTEXT) with one real compilation worker and its actual FIFO queue. Enqueue finite successful ordinary creation jobs in contexts 0 and 1 ahead of a valid parse-only parent-context job (context 2); use known complete serialized/read-back inputs or explicitly complete private create infos.

With timeout_seconds=2, barrier-release individual real jobs and advance only the dispatcher monotonic clock in sub-deadline increments (e.g. 1.5 seconds) through cumulative elapsed time greater than 2 seconds, while completed_count[2] stays zero. Assert every release has actually incremented the production other-context completion count, successful creation/output facts, and that synchronization has not returned or requested timeout/recovery.

Keep the awaited parent job held after ordinary jobs have drained; assert wait remains blocked, requested context queued/completed differ, and its cache/allocator has not been reset/reused. Then release its valid parse, assert its acknowledgement/outcome, exact requested-context drain and natural successful return. Queue completion alone is not success.

Use mutex-protected snapshots and explicit pipe/condition barriers; no sleeps or allocation/CPU/log heuristics determine order. Virtual elapsed time, real completion and native result/explicit assertion state decide the result.

Run the same production FIFO scenario with two actual compilation threads; barriers must acknowledge both workers started and prevent context 2 from completing early even if it was dequeued while an earlier creation remains active.

Assert productive completion in both ordinary contexts beyond the configured elapsed deadline, no premature synchronization, then eventual successful requested-context drain; no per-thread culprit is invented. All real threads are joined and any child reaped.

After at least one acknowledged other-context completion resets the observed work deadline, hold all remaining real jobs; advance controlled monotonic time to just before the configured deadline and then to/above it without any completion.

Assert no early trigger, exactly the work-no-progress origin, configured threshold and actual elapsed/overshoot from the last observed productive snapshot, retained timeout evidence before the real abort/recovery adapter, nonzero/incomplete required work and bounded termination/reap. Productive work must not disable the deadline permanently.
Retain existing ordinary-no-progress and ordinary-delivery-failure controls, plus dispatcher-disabled (zero disables only work deadline), and explicit Release-active assertions.
